key_insight: Filling delignified wood’s cellular pores with polyacrylamide hydrogel enhances compressive strength and toughness through sacrificial bond breakage and proposed mechanical confinement.
engineering_relevance: Wood’s porous architecture offers a route to tougher soft composites by constraining a nearly incompressible hydrogel within cell lumens.
method: Infiltrate delignified wood with polyacrylamide hydrogel.
Evaluate the composites using uniaxial compression tests.
Investigate toughening mechanisms through systematic experiments and theoretical analysis.
evidence_signal: Compression tests showed substantially greater strength and toughness than either constituent alone, although the abstract provides no numerical gains.
watch_item: Performance under repeated loading and deformation modes beyond uniaxial compression remains unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Confinement-induced toughening in delignified wood-polyacrylamide composite hydrogels
